REL-0022.evidence_requirement: State what the observer can and cannot perceive -- side effects produced by a spawned child process, for instance -- and mark the blind region NOT-CHECKED. A zero-hole finding is only as wide as the observer's demonstrated reach, and that reach must be shown before the finding is stated.
inputs: the system-level observer and the measured limits of what it can see
the installer under test, run inside the canary profile
the recorded inverse set standardised by REL-0002
REL-0022.question_or_target: Implementation target: find out what the recorded recovery plan does NOT cover, by watching the installer run instead of by reading the plan. Attach a system-level observer to a genuine install so each side effect it produces is captured as it happens, then subtract the recorded inverse set from the observed side-effect set in both directions. Anything observed but unrecorded is a recovery hole; anything recorded but never observed is a stale entry that will send the next responder somewhere nothing happened. Coverage inferred from reading a document is not coverage.
REL-0022.retry_policy: retry only on a FRESH profile. Re-running a lifecycle drill on a dirtied profile measures the dirt, not the drill; the profile must be destroyed and recreated between attempts
REL-0022.reviewer_requirement: one reviewer whose sole job is to re-run the mutation controls and confirm each one turns the gate red; a reviewer who only re-reads the result has verified nothing
tests_required: Detector control: produce a known side effect and confirm the observer captures it, before any zero-hole finding is entertained.
Introduce an unrecorded side effect into the installer -> the subtraction reports a hole.
Remove a real side effect while leaving its recorded inverse -> the stale-entry direction fires.
Side effects produced by a child process are either captured or declared an uncovered region.
REL-0022.title: Rollback coverage measured by instrumenting a real install, not by reading the manifest
